content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the short term (1-3 days) after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is neutral or flat.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot peaks and fail to correct downward quickly; mean reversion is underemphasized.
- When sentiment is zero (no market sentiment data), model exhibits higher volatility and overconfidence in upward moves.
- In absence of official events, model ignores structural mean reversion and assumes continuation of recent trend.
- If true outcome shows sharp correction after a forecast peak, model should reduce forecast slope and add downward bias for next 3-5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to account for seasonal or policy-driven mean reversion; should anchor to 18-day moving average or prior 30-day median.
- When sentiment is flat, model should not assume momentum; instead, use historical volatility bands or recent range as constraint.
- Overshoots after spikes should be capped at 10-15% above peak for 3-5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If true outcome is below 75% of forecast peak, model should adjust downward by 5-10% for next 7 days unless event-driven.
